speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are suffering from severe abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and difficulty urinating. To help you, I need to ask: where exactly is your pain located, and how severe is it on a scale of 1 to 10?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old female. The patient presents with a 5-day history of severe abdominal pain and cramping, accompanied by nausea and vomiting. She reports pain with urination and also experienced burning pain during sexual intercourse 3 days ago. She mentions being sexually active with one male partner, using condoms inconsistently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID) with possible co-infection.

The patient's history of dysuria, post-coital pain, and sexual activity with inconsistent condom use strongly suggests a sexually transmitted infection ascending to the upper genital tract. I will now request a urine analysis and a pelvic ultrasound to confirm the presence of infection and rule out an abscess. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Urine Culture, STI Panel (Chlamydia/Gonorrhea). REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic_Ultrasound.
